Text: Subclasses in a different package can access protected fields only via {{c1::inheritance}} and not via a {{c2::parent reference}}.
Extra: Accessing them via parent instance reference in a different package triggers a compiler error.

Text: Omitting an access modifier results in {{c1::default}} (or {{c1::package-private}}) visibility, which restricts access to the {{c2::same package}} only.
Extra: Writing `default` as an access modifier on a class field is a syntax error.

Text: Static variables are stored in {{c1::Metaspace}} rather than the {{c2::Heap}}, and only {{c3::one copy}} exists for the entire class.
Extra: Metaspace holds class metadata, which is permanent and shared across all instances.

Text: If an instance synchronized method is called, it acquires the monitor lock on the {{c1::this}} object; a static synchronized method acquires the lock on the {{c2::Class object}}.
Extra: This is why they don't block each other.

Text: The {{c1::volatile}} modifier guarantees visibility by bypassing CPU caches and writing/reading variables directly to/from {{c2::main memory}}.
Extra: It uses memory barriers to enforce visibility and ordering.

Text: To prevent fields from being serialized during Java serialization, they should be marked with the {{c1::transient}} modifier.
Extra: Static fields are automatically excluded from serialization since they belong to class structure.

Text: Methods implemented in other languages like C or C++ are declared in Java using the {{c1::native}} modifier.
Extra: These methods have no Java body and end with a semicolon.

Text: Declaring a class {{c1::final}} prevents it from being extended, while declaring a method {{c2::final}} prevents it from being overridden.
Extra: A class cannot be both abstract and final.

Text: Blank final variables must be definitely assigned in all {{c1::constructors}} before compilation succeeds.
Extra: If left unassigned in even one constructor path, the compiler reports an error.

Text: A static nested class {{c1::does not}} have access to the outer class's {{c2::instance}} fields or methods.
Extra: It behaves exactly like a top-level class nested only for packaging convenience.
